eyebrow: Infrastructure as Code with Terraform · Chapter 4
subtitle: Lesson 19 · Modules & Reuse

eyebrow: A published module, called like any other
code:
module "vpc" {
  source  = "terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws"
  version = "~> 5.0"

  name = "nbretail-dev-vpc"
  cidr = "10.0.0.0/16"

  azs             = ["us-east-1a", "us-east-1b"]
  public_subnets  = ["10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24"]
  private_subnets = ["10.0.101.0/24", "10.0.102.0/24"]

  enable_nat_gateway = true
  single_nat_gateway = true
}
caption: source = "<namespace>/<name>/<provider>" -- no leading ./, this isn't a local path.

code:
$ terraform init

Initializing modules...
Downloading registry.terraform.io/terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws 5.8.1 for vpc...
- vpc in .terraform/modules/vpc

Terraform has been successfully initialized!
caption: Registry modules are resolved during init, exactly like local modules.

eyebrow: Its outputs work the same way
caption: module.vpc.private_subnets -- same module.<name>.<output> syntax as a module you wrote yourself.
